summary: Mobile responsiveness fix verification. Landing Pillar II updates PASS. Mobile scrollWidth == 390 on ALL tabs (tab-wall/journal/breath/guardians/memory) — NO horizontal overflow. However, a CRITICAL runtime error blocks the entire dashboard rendering: MoodChart crashes with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'color')` because historical mood pulses in DB with state `need_help` or `no_talk` are looked up in MOOD_STATES which now has only 3 entries. The overlay error screen covers the page and prevents interaction — mood selector buttons, log-pulse, anchor-link-card, break-glass-card, sos-988-btn all return null in DOM. The agent-to-agent context note explicitly said historical need_help records 'render as orange cells — intentional backward compatibility', but the code has NO fallback for unknown states. Dashboard/health page loads OK. Overflow measurements happen with the error overlay open — real overflow with dashboard content NOT verified.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL runtime crash: `MOOD_STATES[d.state].color` throws TypeError when d.state is a legacy value like 'need_help' or 'no_talk' (historical DB records). Uncaught error overlay covers the entire dashboard, blocking ALL interaction. Mood selector buttons, log-pulse-btn, anchor-link-card, break-glass-card, sos-988-btn cannot be queried because the overlay/error boundary is active. Fix: `const s = MOOD_STATES[d.state]; const c = s ? s.color : (d.state ? '#F7B557' /* orange fallback for legacy */ : 'rgba(76,93,75,0.12)');`

critical_code_review_comments: MoodChart in Dashboard.jsx line 414 does not guard against missing keys in MOOD_STATES lookup. Any reduction of STATES enum must be accompanied by defensive lookup or DB migration. This is the same class of bug as grid-cols-14 — assuming a static shape that DB data may violate.

MOOD_STATES is exported from MoodPulseOrb.jsx but consumed by Dashboard.jsx MoodChart — coupling is fine but a shared `moodStates.js` module + helper `getMoodColor(state)` with fallback would prevent recurrence.

rca of the issue: Root cause: iter-15 reduced MOOD_STATES from 5 entries to 3 (removing need_help, no_talk), but historical mood_pulse records with those states still exist in DB. MoodChart in Dashboard.jsx does an unguarded object lookup `MOOD_STATES[d.state].color` — for legacy states this evaluates to `undefined.color` → TypeError → React error boundary shows a full-page red overlay, which is what testers see instead of the dashboard. Reproduction: load /dashboard with a session that has any pulse whose state is 'need_help' or 'no_talk'. Mitigation: guard the lookup with an existence check and use a fallback color (orange per stated intent) or run a one-time DB migration to remap legacy states to 'struggling'.
